title: Combination of orthokeratology lens with 0.01% atropine in slowing axial elongation in children with myopia: a randomized double-blinded clinical trial

groups.description: orthokeratology (four-zone reverse-geometry lenses, worn about 2 months before baseline) plus 0.01% atropine eye drops once nightly in both eyes from baseline; randomized double-blinded trial, Zhengzhou, China; the 27 analysed of 30 randomised; mean age at enrolment (Tab1)
orthokeratology plus placebo eye drops once nightly from baseline; the 26 analysed of 30 randomised; mean age at enrolment (Tab1)

exclusions.what: Tab1 axial length at enrolment (before ortho-K lens wear, about 3.5 months before the trial baseline)
exclusions.reason: not the trial baseline; the article defines the baseline as the AL after 2 months of ortho-K wear (start of the drops), and the Tab2 series from that baseline is used

exclusions.what: Tab1 age and SER randomisation strata
Tab2 accommodative amplitude and pupil diameter rows; Tab1 SER, keratometry, anterior chamber depth and other characteristics
Interval AL changes as medians [Q1, Q3] and regression estimates (text)
exclusions.reason: medians, interval changes and model estimates are not admissible and are not table cells

exclusions.what: Phase 2 (planned crossover of both groups at the start of the second year)
exclusions.reason: not reported in this article; crossover phases are not extracted (protocol inclusion 8)

notes: Prospective randomized double-blinded placebo-controlled trial (ChiCTR2000033904), First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University, recruited June to September 2020: 60 Han Chinese children aged 8–12 years, SER −1.00 to −4.00 D, astigmatism < 1.50 D, randomised 1:1 after wearing ortho-K lenses successfully for 2 months (stratified by age and SER).

Drops (0.01% atropine or placebo) once nightly in both eyes 10 minutes before lens insertion; because lens delivery took about 1.5 months (COVID-19), drops started about 3.5 months after enrolment, which is the baseline.
AL by IOLMaster (Carl Zeiss Meditec), mean of five measurements; units mm (Tab2); visits every 4 months.

53 of 60 completed 1 year: 3 combination and 4 control children dropped out, including children with poor compliance (excluded per protocol) and children who did not wear ortho-K lenses for more than 1 month; analysis of the right eyes of completers.
